issues.legal_issue: In a suit for permanent injunction, lawful possession should be decided without adjudicating title when title is not framed as an issue and is not genuinely disputed.
material_facts: The suit sought permanent injunction against an attempted encroachment.

The defendants claimed ownership and possession of a different property, acknowledged that other properties lay between it and the suit property, and did not genuinely dispute the plaintiffs’ title to the suit property.
Municipal records, registered conveyances, tax records, and commissioners’ reports supported the plaintiffs’ possession.
The lower courts dismissed the suit after treating the plaintiffs’ failure to establish title as a reason they had not established lawful possession.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs had sufficiently established lawful possession, and the dismissals based on the lower courts’ erroneous focus on title were unsustainable; the appeal was allowed and the dismissals were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Where the relief sought is permanent injunction and title is neither an issue framed for decision nor genuinely disputed, the court should decide the claim by assessing possession and interference rather than unnecessarily adjudicating title. The court relied on the documentary and commissioner evidence in the record; no earlier case was cited for this specific principle.

rule.if: permanent_injunction_suit and title_not_genuinely_disputed and possession_supported_by_evidence and interference_attempted

predicates.permanent_injunction_suit: The claimant brought a civil suit seeking protection of possession by permanent injunction.
predicates.title_not_genuinely_disputed: The opposing party did not genuinely claim title to the property in dispute or pursue a genuine challenge to the claimant’s title.
predicates.possession_supported_by_evidence: Records or other evidence supported the claimant’s possession of the disputed property.
predicates.interference_attempted: The opposing party attempted to interfere with the claimant’s possession.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks a permanent injunction, the opposing party does not genuinely dispute the claimant’s title, possession is supported by evidence, and interference is attempted, the dismissal of the injunction suit is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: Old documents from proper custody and official records may support a claim to property, and should not be rejected without proper grounds when their authenticity is unchallenged and the absence of originals is explained.
material_facts: The plaintiffs produced photocopies of old municipal and other documents after explaining that the originals could not be traced and that efforts to obtain certified copies had failed.
The photocopies were marked as exhibits without objection, and the defendants did not genuinely challenge their authenticity.
The documents were more than thirty years old and came from the plaintiffs’ proper custody.
The record included a certified municipal document and documents concerning municipal acts and conveyances that supported the plaintiffs’ claim.
The lower courts rejected the documents without a valid reason.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the documents was perverse and unsustainable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 114(e) of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 permits a presumption that official acts have been regularly performed, and the burden lies on the person disputing an official act to prove otherwise. Section 90 permits a court, in its discretion, to presume due execution and related matters for a document more than thirty years old produced from proper custody. The court relied on Lakhi Baruah v. Padma Kanta Kalita, (1996) 8 SCC 357, on the Section 90 presumption and its reasoned exercise, and applied those principles to the old records and the explained absence of originals in this case.

rule.if: property_injunction_proceeding and old_documents_from_proper_custody and originals_unavailable_with_explanation and documents_admitted_without_objection and authenticity_not_genuinely_challenged

predicates.property_injunction_proceeding: A party brought a civil proceeding seeking an injunction concerning property.
predicates.old_documents_from_proper_custody: The party produced documents more than thirty years old from custody the court could regard as proper.
predicates.originals_unavailable_with_explanation: The originals or certified copies could not be produced, and the party explained the efforts or circumstances accounting for their absence.
predicates.documents_admitted_without_objection: The documents were marked as evidence without an objection to their admission.
predicates.authenticity_not_genuinely_challenged: The opposing party did not genuinely challenge the authenticity of the documents.

issues.definition: When a party seeking an injunction concerning property produces old documents from proper custody, explains why originals are unavailable, and the documents are admitted without objection and not genuinely challenged as authentic, rejection of that documentary evidence is unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: A court may draw an adverse inference when a party who could testify does not enter the witness box and gives no explanation for not doing so.
material_facts: The original defendant did not appear to testify or submit to cross-examination.
His younger brother testified under a power of attorney and acknowledged that he and the original defendant had separated.
No explanation was given for the original defendant’s failure to testify.
issues.conclusion: An adverse inference was properly drawn against the original defendant.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 114, Illustration (g), of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, the court may draw an adverse inference from a party’s failure to give evidence. The court relied on Iswar Bhai C. Patel v. Harihar Behera, (1999) 3 SCC 457, which states that an adverse presumption is to be drawn where a party does not enter the witness box and present himself for cross-examination.

predicates.civil_property_suit: The proceeding was a civil suit concerning property.
predicates.party_with_relevant_knowledge_did_not_te: A party with relevant knowledge did not enter the witness box or submit to cross-examination.
predicates.failure_to_testify_unexplained: The party gave no explanation for not testifying.

issues.definition: In a civil property suit, when a party with relevant knowledge does not testify and gives no explanation, an adverse inference is drawn against that party.

issues.legal_issue: The identity of property described in a suit is established when municipal records connect its earlier designation to the designation used in the suit.
material_facts: The suit property was described by its current municipal number.
A municipal letter recorded that property sold under earlier site numbers had been renumbered to a number linking it to the property described in the suit.
The lower courts concluded that the identity of the suit property had not been established.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the identity of the suit property had not been established was perverse and unsustainable.
issues.legal_principle: The identity of property may be established by evidence connecting the description in the suit to the property’s earlier municipal designation; the court relied on the municipal renumbering letter in the record. No earlier case was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.property_injunction_suit: A party brought a civil suit for an injunction concerning property.
predicates.municipal_record_links_earlier_designati: A municipal record connects an earlier designation of property to the description used for the property in the suit.

issues.definition: In a property injunction suit, a municipal record linking an earlier designation to the suit’s property description establishes the identity of the property.
